note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a BIS 9, 12; A06b BIS 9, 12; L05 No provision): ordinary naturalisation after 6 years' residence; no renunciation of other citizenships required; a citizen keeps it on taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: by birth in the territory only on the condition the dataset states; by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. The coding also records a restriction to members of a particular group, which the form holds only in the condition's words, which the form doesn't hold. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Guinea-Bissau, 2024
sources.said: Person has been habitually resident in Guinea Bissau for at least 6 years. ... n.a. ... n.a. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Guinea Bissau to a citizen. ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born abroad to a citizen in the service of the state.; Person is born abroad to a citizen and s/he declares that s/he wishes to be a citizen or the birth is recorded in the civil register. ... Group restriction: only if parent is member of a particular group, race or religion ... Person is born in Guinea-Bissau to Lusophone parents. Both parents must be foreign citizens with the citizenship of a Portuguese Speaking State, i.e. Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Equatorial Guinea, Mozambique, Portugal, Sao Tome and Principe, and Timor-Leste. ... No provision
